If confirmed as cSCC (even low-risk), complete excision with margin control (e.g., standard excision with 4–6 mm margins or Mohs micrographic surgery for cosmetically sensitive area) is standard. KA may be managed conservatively *only* with close follow-up and biopsy-proven diagnosis — but excision remains preferred for diagnostic certainty and definitive treatment in the forehead.
